messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: multiple Route healthchecks failing for us-west-2 (AZ-b). Initial spike at 13:02 UTC. Affected: healthcheck-usw2-azb-1, healthcheck-usw2-azb-2. Error pattern: TCP connect timeouts + no metrics reported from synthetic probes. @devon @sara oncall please ack.

devon: acknowledged. I'm taking lead. any customer-facing alerts triggered?

sara: @devon I see ~30 customer requests rerouted with elevated latencies but no 5xx surge in hosted-api; looks like degraded connectivity for a subset of edge nodes in AZ-b. No incident page yet.

mike: oncall-pager duty here — pagerduty shows the alert as "probe-connect-failure" noise from Route checks. PD incident created: INC-4521. I set priority to P2 pending triage.

devon: quick checklist — 1) confirm probe telemetry gap 2) try direct curl to healthcheck endpoints from jumpbox in AZ-b 3) check probe agent logs (kgc) 4) decide failover if necessary. Starting step 1.

beth: logs show probe agent last heartbeat at 13:01:58 UTC, then nothing. Metric stream to prometheus gateway stopped. snippet from gateway logs:

```
2026-03-15T13:02:04Z WARN connection reset by peer from 10.12.45.7
2026-03-15T13:02:05Z ERROR write tcp 10.12.45.7:443 -> 54.182.33.9:52314: write: no route to host
```

lina: running curl from a control-plane host in us-west-2 AZ-a to the probe endpoint in AZ-b:

```
curl -v http://10.12.45.7:8080/health
*   Trying 10.12.45.7...
* connect to 10.12.45.7 port 8080 failed: Connection timed out
```

devon: tcpdump from a bastion in AZ-b shows SYNs with no replies to public egress IPs — looks like asymmetric egress/drop. grabbing packet capture and pushing to incident channel.

incident-bot: uploaded files: pcap-usw2-azb-1303.pcap (redacted).

sara: contacted cloud provider support (ticket CP-9834). They responded: "we are investigating edge router controller events in us-west-2, some BGP session flaps observed affecting egress from AZ-b". They ask for packet capture and traceroutes.

devon: running traceroute to 8.8.8.8 from a host in AZ-b:

```
traceroute to 8.8.8.8 (8.8.8.8), 30 hops max
 1  10.12.45.1 (10.12.45.1)  0.371 ms 0.302 ms 0.277 ms
 2  * * *
 3  * * *
```

mike: this explains missing telemetry — if egress is flaky, our probe agents can’t push to the metrics gateway or Route53 checks. We should assume probes in AZ-b are unreliable until CP confirms.

beth: recommendation: mark AZ-b as degraded in routing config and shift synthetic-checks to AZ-a / AZ-c. Also consider toggling healthcheck weight to avoid flapping. I'll prepare canary route change.

devon: agree. Plan: 1) update traffic router to prefer AZ-a/c for synthetic and customer egress for 15min 2) continue capturing metrics 3) escalate to SRE lead if CP can't give ETA in 15min 4) notify customer-ops with initial impact note. Executing step 1 now.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: Rolling update to routing policy "prefer-usw2-azac" started by devon at 13:18 UTC.

sara: update: PD incident INC-4521 annotated with customer impact: "Subset of customers in us-west-2 saw increased request latencies and delayed telemetry between 13:02-13:18 UTC. No global request failures reported. Ongoing." Posting to status page (draft) for review.

lina: after routing change, I see probes from AZ-b still show intermittent connectivity, but overall probe volume for the region recovered as traffic routed away. Prometheus scraping resumed from AZ-a/c.

mike: cloud-support-bot posted: "Root cause suspected: edge BGP controller churn causing intermittent egress blackholing from AZ-b. Our network engineers are applying mitigations and will provide update within 30 minutes." CP ticket CP-9834 updated.

beth: created follow-up playbook item: add synthetic probes that originate outside AZ-b to detect asymmetric-egress earlier. Filing as ENG-PL-224.

devon: writing customer-facing timeline and impact now. Key points: timeline, affected AZ, mitigation steps (routing preference), no data loss, metric gaps explained, next steps. Anyone want to add notes?

sara: add note that some internal alerting was noisy due to missing telemetry — we've disabled the noise rule for healthchecks until CP confirms stability.

devon: handing off to @mike for night-oncall at 13:40 UTC. I will remain available for escalation. Handoff note: CP investigating BGP controller, routing policy set to prefer AZ-a/c, monitor for recurrence, PD INC-4521, CP-9834. Mike ack?

mike: ack. Taking over. I'll keep PD watch and update status page at 13:55 with CP ETA. If we see new failures, page immediately.

cloud-support-bot: CP-9834 update at 13:51 UTC: "Applying control-plane stability patch to affected routers; expected reduction in flap events within 20m. Monitoring." 

mike: adding retrospective tasks: improve runbook for asymmetric egress, ensure probe agent retries/alternate egress logic, update synthetic coverage. Added to ENG-SRE backlog.

incident-bot: Incident INC-4521 moved to mitigated state by mike at 14:30 UTC. Final notes: traffic reroute held, metric ingestion resumed, CP reports stability. Will keep monitoring for 2h.

devon: closing comments: good coordination, quick routing mitigation prevented broader customer impact. Follow-up: schedule postmortem with cloud provider liaison and include packet captures and traceroutes. Thanks team :thumbsup:
